note: The third of the quince#290 set, and the one that keeps the transition test from over-narrowing. Found in review of the fix: keying the transition on null-vs-non-null means BOTH observations can be answered while describing DIFFERENT blocks — a reviewer requests changes and the author answers, both inside one interval — and nothing fires. That is a MISSED wake, which is the expensive direction: a spurious wake costs one drain, a missing one costs a review that never happens. Not hypothetical — the only two-verdicts-in-one-interval case in this project's history was 79 s apart, well inside a 90 s tick. So the key is the BLOCK, not the boolean: fire when `blocked_at` differs from the one already reported. THE THREE FIXTURES ARE A SET AND NONE IS REDUNDANT: issue282-a-blocked-pr-the-author-answered proves it fires when the condition becomes true, issue290-review-answered-does-not-repeat proves it stays silent while one block persists, and this proves it fires again for a NEW block. The pre-fix code passed the first; the null-vs-non-null fix passed the first two.
